header.title: AI terms in plain English
header.subtitle: The technical words on our site, explained in everyday language. If a term is missing, ask us and we will add it.

terms.plain: Software that does a task for you, such as drafting replies or processing invoices, and checks with a person before anything important.
The point where a person signs off before the agent sends, spends or deletes anything.
The kind of AI behind ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. It reads and writes text, and it is the "brain" an agent uses.
An AI model that runs on your own machines, so your data never leaves.
An engineer who works alongside your team, inside your systems, until it works.
How the AI plugs into your existing tools, such as your CRM, email or finance system. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a common standard for this.
A way for two pieces of software to talk to each other directly, without a person copying data between them.
Letting the AI look things up in your own documents before it answers, so answers are based on your facts.
When an AI states something that sounds right but is not true. Looking things up in your documents and having a person check important answers keeps this in check.
Security and speed protection that blocks attacks and overload before they reach your systems, and serves pages quickly.
A secure front door for your systems: every request passes through it and is checked first.

terms.term: CI/CD and int, test, acc and prod
terms.plain: Updates are tested in stages (integration, test, acceptance) before they reach your live system (production).
Passwords and keys are locked away, and every time one is used it is recorded.
We can see what each agent did, how long it took and what it cost.
Runs completely offline, with no internet connection.
The smallest version that does the real job on your real data, so you can see it working before you commit to the full build.
Our target: each person gets ten times more done on the work we automate.
